newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX edges up to a new high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX edges up to a new high.

text.p: Hungarian share prices traded mixed with losers outnumbering gainers by the end of the session in an apparent profit-taking after an over 30 percent rise of the market this year, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 5,499.74 points, up 3.18.
The index was propelled primarily by oil and gas company MOL shares which continued to surge to new highs, amid some profit-taking, they said.
"MOL continued to strenghten, although there was some profit-taking," Gabor Temesvari of Procent Hungaria said.
MOL opened at 3,295 forints, above Monday's close of 3,200 and rallied to a new peak of 3,480 forints before retreating to close at 3,425, up 225.
Some traders warned that this rally might be too rapid ahead of a new phase in MOL's privatisation.
"I think MOL's price is very high," one trader said earlier today, adding that "my perception is that MOL cannot be sold at this price." "This price rise is a hysteria."
Most other shares moved downward amid profit-taking which was regarded only short-lived.
"Profit-taking pulled shares lower but this profit-taking ended today," Temesvari said.
The two chemicals stocks slipped a shade lower, with Borsodchem closing at 5,965 forints, down 25 and TVK at 2,525, down 20.
The pharmaceuticals were mixed, with Human ending steady at 3,350 forints, Richter advancing 50 forints to 11,000 and Egis falling 500 forints to 11,000.
The bank papers moved lower, with OTP plummeting six and a half percent or 240 forints to 3,450 and Inter-Europa Bank to 55,500, down 1,500.

Home improvement product maker Graboplast which said it had lodged an order for the sale via the bourse of 4,730 own shares, fell 245 forints to end at 8,550, while plastics maker Pannonplast dipped 10 forints to 7,100.

The market failed to take much advantage from the strong dollar with many of the stocks slipping below Monday's close from the day's peaks, but the U.S. currency might help on Wednesday, traders said.
"The stronger dollar points towards an upwards trend tomorrow," Temesvari said.
